paper.title_en: Half-lives of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>183</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>185</mn></mmultiscripts></math> from electron-induced reactions on natural tungsten
paper.abstract_en: New high-precision measurements of the half-lives of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>183</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>185</mn></mmultiscripts></math> are presented. Accurate half-life data are important for testing nuclear-structure models and for providing reliable nuclear-physics input to astrophysical reaction-network calculations. The isotopes were produced via photonuclear reactions involving proton emission induced by bremsstrahlung generated with a 24-MeV electron beam from the linear accelerator at the National Centre for Nuclear Research. The decay of the reaction products was monitored using high-purity germanium detectors, and the half-lives were determined from the time evolution of <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray peak-area ratios relative to selected reference transitions over multiple half-life periods. The obtained half-lives are <math><mrow><mn>5.0817</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0023</mn><mspace width="4pt"/><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></math> for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>183</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mrow><mn>47.936</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.016</mn><mspace width="4pt"/><mi>min</mi></mrow></math> for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>185</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. These results represent the most precise half-life measurements reported to date, improving the precision of the previous measurements by approximately two orders of magnitude.
